instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Cut the cauliflower into florets about 1 inch across. Pat them dry.

Transfer the florets to a rimmed baking sheet. Add 2 tbsp of the oil, the cumin, coriander, chili powder, smoked paprika and 3/4 tsp of the salt and toss. Spread them in a single layer, flat sides down, with space between the pieces.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once at the 15 minute mark, until the edges are deep brown and a knife slides in easily.
Meanwhile, thinly slice half the cabbage. That should be about 3 cups. Transfer it to a bowl and toss with the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the juice of 1 lime and 1/4 tsp of the salt.

Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro. In a small bowl, stir together the sour cream, 1 tbsp juice from the second lime, 2 tbsp of the chopped cilantro, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and 2 tbsp water. It should be thin enough to drizzle. Cut the rest of the second lime into wedges.
Warm a dry skillet over medium-high. Heat each tortilla for 20 seconds on each side, then stack them in a clean towel.
Squeeze a lime wedge over the hot cauliflower. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Fill each tortilla with a spoonful of the slaw and some cauliflower. Drizzle with the lime crema and top with the rest of the chopped cilantro. Serve with the lime wedges.
method_notes: Love & Lemons (5.0 from 25 ratings) is the lead: cauliflower roasted with cumin, coriander and salt on corn tortillas with a cool green sauce. Inspired Taste and Kathleen Ashmore agree on roasting at 425°F in a single layer and on a lime crema or sauce, and add chili powder and smoked paprika. They differ on the sauce (sour cream crema versus avocado) and on whether the cabbage is roasted. Changed: the dish calls for a lime crema, so the sauce is sour cream with lime, and the red cabbage is kept raw as a crunchy slaw rather than roasted with the cauliflower.
